top.title: England Records 5,258 Heat-Linked Deaths This Summer- Health Agency
top.description: England registered 5,258 deaths linked to this summer’s heat, the highest number of such fatalities on record, the UK’s Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said in estimates released Tuesday. “Summer 2026 was an exceptional summer, with the highest mortality observed since 2016, when the UKHSA began publishing annual heat mortality reports,” the agency said in a provisional report. Britain experienced its hottest summer on record this year, characterised by early and successive heatwaves. The country has also seen an exceptional drought that resulted from a lack of rainfall not seen in nearly 200 years. Scientists say human-driven climate change is amplifying extreme weather events, with Europe warming faster than the global average and heatwaves growing more frequent and severe. While the provisional figures may be revised, the mortality impact “exceeds that observed in any previous annual heat-associated mortality estimate”, the UKHSA added. People use emergency blankets to protect themselves from the heat as they arrive at the Olympic stadium for a concert of US singer Bruno Mars on June 28, 2026, in Berlin. (Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP) The latest figure, logged across seven “heat episodes” between May and September, topples the previous record of 2,985 estimated heat-linked deaths in summer 2022. The UKHSA analysis compares mortality during periods of heat with mortality during “nearby non-heat periods”, the agency said. This is particularly useful for understanding the impacts of heatwaves, it added. Multiple European countries registered record heat-related deaths after a sweltering summer this year, including Germany with 16,300 and more than 5,000 in Spain. A report published in The Lancet medical journal last month said climate change must be declared a “global health emergency” and found there were more than three million deaths caused by heat between 2016 and 2023. Tourists shield themselves from the sun with umbrellas at St Peter’s Square in the Vatican during a heatwave, on June 24, 2026. (Photo by Filippo MONTEFORTE / AFP) Heat-related excess deaths often result from the higher risk of heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable. Britain’s national weather agency has predicted the El Nino weather pattern could make 2027 the hottest year globally. Experts are urging the country to better prepare homes and public infrastructure for warmer summers. top.title: Freshman phenom Tim Ibukunoluwa off to historic start for Siena
top.description: Siena's Tim Ibukunoluwa (13) drives past St. John's Reed Bailey (13) during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, in the Queens borough of New York. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II) (Frank Franklin II/Associated Press) ALBANY - Only six games into his college basketball career, Siena freshman Tim Ibukunoluwa is making Metro Conference history. He was named Metro Player and Rookie of the Week on Monday for the third time in as many weeks to begin the season. He's the first Metro freshman to win three Player of the Week honors in an entire season in the 47-year history of the league. "I kind of just try not to look at it," Ibukunoluwa said before practice. "I know what my goal is. My goal is to win every single game, win the Metro and get to the tournament. That (awards) stuff isn't really any of my goals, but obviously, it's nice for it to come with it. So I'm just looking at the wins." Siena fans will get to see the 6-foot-8 Australian phenom in person again when the Saints take on the University of Vermont at 7 p.m. Tuesday at MVP Arena. He's tied for fourth in the country at 25.2 points per game and ranks ninth at 10.5 rebounds per contest. In Saturday's 93-87 win at Bucknell , Ibukunoluwa finished with 34 points, 15 rebounds and six assists to become the first Division I freshman with at least 30 points, 15 rebounds and five assists in a game since the 1938-39 season, when the NCAA Tournament began, according to the data sites CBB Analytics and Stathead. He's the first Metro player in any class to win three straight Player of the Week awards since Iona's Nelly Junior Joseph won four in a row from Dec. 12, 2022 to Jan. 2, 2023. "He's been awesome with (the attention)," Siena coach Nevada Smith said. "He understands it. He's such a team-first guy. He just cares about winning and that's been his whole thing the whole time. He's just doing what it takes to help our team win and whatever comes to him is definitely well-deserved, but he's handled it really well." Ibukunoluwa also scored 16 points in last Wednesday's loss at St. John's. Red Storm coaching legend Rick Pitino said after that game that Ibukunoluwa has "great potential" and should stay at Siena as a sophomore to develop rather than transferring to a higher-level program for more money. Ibukunoluwa said he and his family haven't mapped out a long-term plan. "They just want the best for me and I want the best for myself," Ibukunoluwa said. "Just staying at a school that's going to have good development, that's going to push me and just to play somewhere I'm very comfortable and that I'm always trying to work and improve myself." Asked if he's worried about bigger schools trying to tamper with Ibukunoluwa, Smith replied, "Oh, for sure, they already try." "It's the worst thing about having a really good player at our level," Smith said. If you’re struggling for gift ideas, you will find unexpected and ingenious suggestions for amateur astronomers and animal and nature lovers, as well as those fond of food, beauty and puzzles. And surely that covers all of us? But if you want something that’s part puzzle, part work of art, and that will keep you transfixed for hours, they’ll definitely do the trick. Nervous System makes laser-cut wooden puzzles with uniquely shaped pieces and science themes, and they are absolutely beautiful. top.title: How weird vibes from the Springboks could have huge impact in Nations Championship final
top.description: To whatever extent the words of Rassie Erasmus were lost in translation last week, South Africa used their team announcement press conference on Monday to make a clear point. With Erasmus unable to conduct media duties under the terms of his ban from World Rugby , assistant coach Mzwandile Stick stood in at the Springboks ’ hotel in southwest London – taking questions in English but answering only in Xhosa, his first language. It was explained that the coaching staff wanted to ensure nothing was misinterpreted. With the dedicated Kuhle Sonkosi – a former lock who now works for South African broadcaster SuperSport – acting as an impromptu translator, Stick spent a slightly stilted half-an-hour explaining a heavily-changed team for the Nations Championship final against France. He espoused the virtues of Manu Tshituka, the Congo-born back rower compared to Pieter-Steph du Toit primed for an international debut at Twickenham on Sunday. Mzwandile Stick conducted his press briefing entirely in Xhosa (PA) At one point, Stick cracked a joke about his good looks being the reason he attracted more attention than other coaches from the cameras in Dublin, insisting that it had been a collective effort to replace Erasmus. To Sonkosi’s credit, the remark drew a chuckle even on translation. Clearly, the coach was entitled to converse in his mother tongue if he wished to; South Africa has 12 official languages, of course. As is generally the case, he was engaging company. Stick (left) stood in for Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus (Getty) Yet one could should not shake a slightly peculiar feel. In part, that has to do with a side going into a final, with two trophies potentially on the line, on the heels of consecutive defeats. “Obviously, it’s not ideal to go into the final having lost back-to-back losses,” Stick admitted. “I think the more we’re frustrated at is that we haven’t played to our standards. For us, it’s very important to stop this run.” A shot at revenge against France is welcome after a game of fine margins; the Springboks coach rightly noted that his side had come out on the right side of three one-point contests on their way to World Cup glory two years ago. But the weirdness pervaded beyond the oddities of this new competition. top.title: Jaime Jaquez Jr. Still Fits Miami Heat Culture Despite Trade
top.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The trade sent Jaime Jaquez Jr. to Milwaukee, yet the Miami Heat connection never truly broke. He returned to the Kaseya Center on November 18 wearing a Bucks jersey and played with the same grit Miami fans love. With the Heat securing a 137–130 victory, he tallied 10 points and dished out five assists to lead his team in that matchup. According to local reports from Ethan Skolnick, insiders and fans are already anticipating a potential reunion as soon as he becomes available. Jaquez has not lost his edge in his first 18 games with the Bucks. He is averaging 14.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 2.9 assists while shooting 42.5% from three-point range. Yahoo Sports notes that his performance has cemented the view that he personifies the traits characterizing “Heat culture.” This culture relies on physicality, downhill pressure, and a willingness to do the dirty work without needing special plays drawn up. Why The Heat Still Want Him Back Miami values players who fit their specific identity, and Jaquez fits it perfectly. His blue-collar mentality matches the ethos the franchise demands from every single player on the roster. Although the Bucks hold the reins on his restricted free agency and any extension discussions, the connection between his style and Miami’s requirements persists. The front office knows that a player who works hard and plays tough is exactly what they need to win again. Fans will keep watching his progress closely as the season unfolds. Should the trade market change, they seek an opportunity to bring him back to South Florida. His stats show he can score and defend, which are the two most important things for a Heat forward. A Look At The Current Roster The Heat are also finding their own rhythm with other young players. Nikola Jovic is carving out a role thanks to his defensive tenacity, though his shooting splits are still low at 32.4/25.0/78.6. Meanwhile, Davion Mitchell has become a key piece after joining in the Jimmy Butler trade. He is averaging 17 points and 8.6 assists while shooting 51% from the field. Mitchell’s ascent has aided the Heat throughout their ongoing seven-game winning streak. Dwyane Wade praised his work ethic on his YouTube channel, noting that Mitchell travels with a basketball everywhere he goes as a grown man. “A guy that walks around and travel with a basketball everywhere he goes as a grown man, I’m rocking with him,” said Wade. The Heat have a clear path forward with players who love the game and work hard. Whether Jaquez returns or not, the team has found a way to keep its core values alive. The roster is built on players who understand what it takes to succeed in Miami. Jaquez recorded 10 points and five assists in his return game on November 18.

top.title: Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana hits out at Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe critics and demands respect for 'killer' former PSG superstar
top.description: Kylian Mbappe - Getty Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has mounted a passionate defence of Kylian Mbappe's Ligue 1 record, insisting his international team-mate's achievements are far too often downplayed. The French centre-back also sparked debate by comparing Mbappe at his peak to Brazilian icon Neymar. Fofana leaps to defence of Mbappe's French legacy Fofana has passionately defended Mbappe's record in Ligue 1, arguing that the forward's achievements in France are frequently trivialised. Speaking as a guest on the YouTube show Zack en Roue Libre , the French centre-back insisted that critics fail to appreciate the true scale of Mbappe's dominance during his time in his homeland. Mbappe rose through the youth academy at Monaco before spending seven prolific years at PSG. Despite his extraordinary goalscoring output across those seasons, Fofana believes public perception has unfairly downplayed his domestic exploits. Chelsea star compares prime Mbappe to Neymar To illustrate Mbappe's brilliance, Fofana weighed the French superstar against his former PSG star Neymar, placing the Brazilian just behind football's two greatest modern icons. However, the Chelsea defender maintained that Mbappe's relentless efficiency in Ligue 1 matched Neymar's peak level. "If you take Mbappe in his prime and Neymar in his prime, it is a close contest," Fofana said. "Neymar is the ultimate player after CR7 and Messi. But what I saw from Mbappe in Ligue 1 was insane. We trivialise what he did far too much." A dominant seven-year spell in the French capital After bursting onto the scene with Monaco, Mbappe seven-year stint at PSG saw him deliver relentless consistency week after week in Ligue 1. Having faced the challenge of defending against top-level attackers himself, Fofana offered a player's perspective on how difficult it is to maintain that standard. By labelling Mbappe a "hitman", the Chelsea defender emphasised the ruthless predictability of his goalscoring rather than sheer spectacle. "Mbappe is a hitman; every weekend it's a goal," he noted. "With Neymar, there is the flair, the madness, because you tell yourself, 'imagine if he had been serious'." Debate continues over Mbappe's place among football's elite Fofana's candid assessment is sure to fuel ongoing debates among supporters regarding how Mbappe's years in France should be judged alongside his peers. What is certain is that Mbappe will continue his campaign with Real Madrid this season, with Los Blancos set to face PSV in the Champions League. Meanwhile, Fofana will look to help the Blues secure a victory as they travel to face Nottingham Forest in the Premier League this weekend.

According to Anfield Watch, the thinking at Anfield is increasingly focused on depth behind Florian Wirtz, whose recent form has underlined both his importance and the need for smart cover. The original report states that Liverpool are “exploring moves to sign a back-up for the German international” and that the club are now “ramping up moves to sign a back-up for Wirtz in the January window”. IMAGO Florian Wirtz Form Driving Liverpool Planning There is a straightforward logic to this. Liverpool are pleased with Wirtz and the numbers support that stance. As reported, he “created 10 chances against Man United all by himself” and now has “four assists and six goals in his last nine starts for club and country”. Those returns offer a strong indication of why he remains central to the attacking structure. Internally, there appears to be an acceptance that elite talent still needs protection. The report says Ward and the recruitment staff “are well aware that Wirtz needs a deputy. Liverpool cannot rely on him alone.” That line feels important. Recruitment at top clubs is rarely about replacing quality already in the building, it is about insulating it, sustaining it and ensuring the level does not drop across a long season. Abdellah Ouazane Emerges on Liverpool Shortlist Among the names under consideration, Ouazane stands out. Anfield Watch reports that “the Moroccan attacking midfielder who plays for Ajax has also been looked at by the Reds and is a serious candidate.” For Liverpool, that profile makes immediate sense. Ouazane is described as a player with versatility and projection. He has operated from the left, though he is also characterised as “a traditional no.10” and someone who “has also been deployed as a no.8 at youth level”. That positional flexibility has become increasingly valuable in modern recruitment, especially for clubs looking to future-proof several roles with one signing. The background is compelling too. He has “already represented Morocco at senior international level despite being only 17-years-old” and is “regarded as one of the best Ajax prospects to have come through the club’s prestigious academy in the last decade”. top.title: Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt demolish Australia as England level T20 series
top.description: England’s all-Welsh opening partnership of Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt annihilated Australia with a brutal display of power hitting to level the T20 series in style on the Gold Coast. The pair rained down 13 sixes on the Carrara Oval in a frenzied stand of 151 that saw them make a target of 185 look like child’s play, speeding to an eight-wicket thrashing with 6.5 overs unused. The silent partner of the England and Wales Cricket Board made itself known in no uncertain terms after a false start in Melbourne on Saturday, with Swansea-born Donald blitzing 85 in 32 balls and Salt – who traded Denbighshire for Barbados as a schoolboy – adding 58 off 30. It was a devastating display which left some nasty scars on a pieced-together Australia attack that performed impressively to go 1-0 ahead at the MCG. Nikhil Chaudhary was taken apart by Donald in the fifth over, leaking 26 runs, before left-armer Joel Davies suffered even more grievously at Salt’s hands. Phil Salt batting for England on the Gold Coast (Dave Hunt/AAPImage via AP) His second over disappeared for an excruciating 31, including four sixes, a boundary and three skittish wides as he tried to hide the ball from his tormentor. Donald was hurtling towards a century when he picked out the catcher at long-on but, having scored just 56 runs in his first four innings during an uncertain start to his international career, this was no time for regrets. Salt also fell before the end, courtesy of a brilliant one-handed caught-and-bowled by Ben Dwarshuis, but their bullying partnership meant that was little more than damage-limitation. Tom Banton finished it off from the first ball of the 13th over, clearing the ropes for the third time in his own eight-ball cameo to end Australia’s pain. Despite the dominant nature of the chase, Australia would have been relatively content at the changeover, carving out 184 for eight on an unpredictable drop-in pitch. It turned out to be nowhere near enough but, after nailing 50 off the last three overs and watching Ben Dwarshuis end the innings with three consecutive sixes off Sam Curran , they had made their charge. England began by handing a debut to James Coles, who was immediately tasked with the first over of the day. He settled quickly by allowing just five singles, but that was a calm moment in an otherwise manic powerplay, during which Australia swung their way to 58 at the cost of four wickets. top.title: “Your Job to Create That Environment”: Fans Blame Lane Kiffin as He Criticizes Players for Playing for Themselves Ahead of Bowl Games
top.description: Louisiana State Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin. © Reuters LSU’s chances of making the college football playoffs are done and dusted, and with pressure on Lane Kiffin to justify the huge price tag that came with his appointment, the head coach would want his team to end on a high with the bowl games coming up. But Kiffin believes that players are only playing for themselves in the NIL era, pointing out the challenges that come with this generation. “They’re going to play for themselves and so if they put out bad film, they make bad decisions, they don’t hustle on a play, or they don’t play well, they’re hurting themselves whether that’s here or whether that’s somewhere else next year when they go to negotiate,” he said. Kiffin’s comments weren’t necessarily echoed by fans, with one saying, “He’s going to need a lot of talent to win with this attitude, it’s your job to create that environment in this landscape of college football it’s not easy for reasons he stated but you got to find that or LSU is going to have a budget bigger than anyone else and by a good margin.” Lane Kiffin Apologized for Using Profanity in a Halftime Interview Lane Kiffin recently used some foul language at halftime on LSU’s radio network during the game against Tennessee, and was quick to apologize for his comments after LSU’s safety Ty Benefield was ejected for targeting. “I want to apologize for my language at halftime in the interview,” Kiffin said to reporters. “No excuses. I was frustrated with the first half and really couldn’t even hear the question, kind of like our center down in the student section. But there’s no reason for that. And so, to people who were offended, I apologize for that.” Kiffin also pointed out one core issue he wants to address with this LSU team. “I keep saying, ‘I’m not concerned about the future of the program. I’m excited about the future of the program, but we have one core issue to fix, and that’s how we finish games. We’re in these games against really, really good teams, and we don’t play well late, and that can be part of a mindset that we don’t have right.” LSU plays Arkansas this Saturday in Fayetteville. Serving a long suspension from La Liga for a red card he picked up against Villarreal, the Brazilian star slowly saw his place being taken over by Yan Diomande, whom the manager slowly began viewing as an option on the left flank. With the team’s results also improving after the forced change, it slowly began to become clear that Vinicius was no longer as irreplaceable as he had been over the years. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) For a long time, Vinicius’ situation this season seemed hopeless and his arc appeared to only be moving downhill. In Brazil’s two games in the recent hiatus, Vinicius scored five goals including a hat-trick and a brace, putting aside his poor form and rediscovering his goalscoring boots. He started on the bench at the weekend, but his cameo was powerful and even played a critical part in Real Madrid’s comeback. nigeria.title: England Records 5,258 Heat-Linked Deaths This Summer- Health Agency
nigeria.description: England registered 5,258 deaths linked to this summer’s heat, the highest number of such fatalities on record, the UK’s Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said in estimates released Tuesday. “Summer 2026 was an exceptional summer, with the highest mortality observed since 2016, when the UKHSA began publishing annual heat mortality reports,” the agency said in a provisional report. Britain experienced its hottest summer on record this year, characterised by early and successive heatwaves. The country has also seen an exceptional drought that resulted from a lack of rainfall not seen in nearly 200 years. Scientists say human-driven climate change is amplifying extreme weather events, with Europe warming faster than the global average and heatwaves growing more frequent and severe. While the provisional figures may be revised, the mortality impact “exceeds that observed in any previous annual heat-associated mortality estimate”, the UKHSA added. People use emergency blankets to protect themselves from the heat as they arrive at the Olympic stadium for a concert of US singer Bruno Mars on June 28, 2026, in Berlin. (Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP) The latest figure, logged across seven “heat episodes” between May and September, topples the previous record of 2,985 estimated heat-linked deaths in summer 2022. The UKHSA analysis compares mortality during periods of heat with mortality during “nearby non-heat periods”, the agency said. This is particularly useful for understanding the impacts of heatwaves, it added. Multiple European countries registered record heat-related deaths after a sweltering summer this year, including Germany with 16,300 and more than 5,000 in Spain. A report published in The Lancet medical journal last month said climate change must be declared a “global health emergency” and found there were more than three million deaths caused by heat between 2016 and 2023. Tourists shield themselves from the sun with umbrellas at St Peter’s Square in the Vatican during a heatwave, on June 24, 2026. (Photo by Filippo MONTEFORTE / AFP) Heat-related excess deaths often result from the higher risk of heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable. Britain’s national weather agency has predicted the El Nino weather pattern could make 2027 the hottest year globally. Experts are urging the country to better prepare homes and public infrastructure for warmer summers. The President also forwarded a revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework to the House for consideration and approval. In a letter read on the floor of the House on Tuesday by the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu said the proposed adjustments were aimed at aligning the 2026 budget with existing obligations and available resources. Under the revised fiscal framework, aggregate expenditure stands at N65.176tn, down from the N68.323tn approved in the original budget, while projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, is put at N33.720tn. The revised budget also provides for aggregate capital expenditure of N26.232tn, while retaining the fiscal deficit of N31.457tn, representing 5.64 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product. Tinubu explained that the proposed adjustments would regularise some Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited expenditures incurred on behalf of the Federation, address underprovided debt-service obligations and recognise issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments. He said the revised framework would also provide for refunds to ministries, departments and agencies, as well as special accounts. According to the president, MDA capital provisions consist mainly of amounts already warranted, while a few new capital and overhead provisions were introduced as priority national interventions. He listed the interventions to include the completion of critical road projects, protection of agricultural production, reduction of production costs, improvement of farm yields, enhanced market access and measures to address water vulnerability. On borrowing, the President said the planned new borrowing remained unchanged at N29.218tn, comprising N18.428tn in domestic borrowing and N10.790tn in foreign borrowing. He further disclosed that the proposed $7.7bn external borrowing, equivalent to approximately N10.368tn at an exchange rate of N1,346.50 to the dollar, was intended to finance the existing foreign borrowing provision and would not increase the borrowing envelope. Tinubu said the adjustments were designed to prioritise existing commitments, improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget and maintain fiscal restraint. He consequently appealed to the lawmakers for expeditious consideration and passage of the bill to facilitate the orderly implementation of the revised budget and settlement of outstanding obligations. nigeria.title: Nigeria can’t borrow its way out of economic crisis – Duke
nigeria.description: The presidential candidate of Peoples Redemption Party, PRP, Donald Duke, has warned that Nigeria cannot borrow its way out of its economic crisis, urging the federal government to shift from debt-driven spending to policies capable of expanding production, creating wealth and strengthening the country’s revenue base. Duke, who was former governor of Cross River State, spoke in an interview in Abuja against the backdrop of the country’s rising debt burden and persistent economic pressures on households and businesses. He said: “Borrowing is not inherently wrong, but the critical question is what borrowed funds were being used for and whether they were generating sufficient economic returns. “Nigeria cannot continue contracting loans simply to sustain an economic structure that is failing to produce enough wealth and revenue. “Borrowing could be justified where funds were invested in productive infrastructure and other ventures capable of expanding the economy, but not using debt to finance inefficiency or recurrent expenditure.” Duke said the country must instead focus on increasing productivity, improving the business environment and expanding the number of Nigerians and businesses participating meaningfully in the formal economy. The PRP presidential candidate argued that Nigeria’s fiscal challenge was ultimately a production problem. “A country that does not produce enough cannot generate the revenue required to meet its obligations, regardless of how much money it borrows. “There is a need for a fundamental review of government expenditure. Public funds should be directed towards investments that increase productivity, create employment and generate additional revenue. “Government should broaden the revenue base without imposing measures that further weaken households and businesses. “The objective should be to create an economy in which businesses grow, employment expands and government revenues increase naturally as economic activity increases. “Continuing to rely heavily on borrowing without addressing these structural weaknesses would simply shift today’s problems to future generations,”he warned. The former Cross River governor said Nigeria needed to move away from an economic model centered on finding money to sustain government towards one focused on creating wealth. He said the country did not merely need more money in government coffers but a stronger productive economy capable of generating the resources required to finance development. “As a presidential candidate, I am concerned not merely with managing the current economic crisis but with changing the underlying structure that repeatedly produces it. “Nigerians deserve an economic system capable of creating sustainable opportunities rather than one that continually responds to hardship after it has occurred,” he said. nigeria.title: Questions Linger After Jensen Huang’s Return To Nvidia
nigeria.description: Jensen Huang’s surprise return to Nvidia on Monday appeared to stabilize the US chip giant, along with the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, but questions linger about the longterm impact of his scandal. Is Nvidia in the clear? An internal investigation overseen by independent directors is still underway at Nvidia regarding concerns that Huang might have been the target of an espionage campaign by China. US government officials, including President Donald Trump, assured Nvidia’s board that reinstating the company’s cofounder “poses no national security risk.” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP In parallel, the US Department of Justice is investigating Megaspeed, a company based in Singapore that allegedly bought processors from Nvidia and routed them to Chinese customers, circumventing US export restrictions. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has also reportedly launched an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices and potentially misleading communication to shareholders. However, the Trump administration has generally avoided going after its allies, so the federal probes might not result in much, Columbia University Professor Eric Talley said. Will Huang be held accountable? Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. The embattled chief will nevertheless have to explain himself to lawmakers at a closed-door hearing on December 1 before three House committees. He will also testify before a Senate committee on December 3 in a hearing that will be livestreamed, while California’s attorney general has opened an investigation into the company’s chip exports and shareholder disclosures. There are plenty of regulators who are willing to push back against the Trump administration and ask tough questions, Talley said. Trump is also known to flip on people whom he no longer considers friends. “He can become estranged with people, and if that would happen with Jensen Huang, I can imagine a boomerang” on the Trump administration’s approach, Talley said. What does the board’s future look like? The logo of Nvidia is seen during a production preview exhibition in Taipei on May 21, 2025. Photo by I-HWA CHENG / AFP Openly opposed to Huang’s return before ultimately reinstating him, the board is in a delicate position. Former Goldman Sachs chief Lloyd Blankfein predicts its days may be numbered. A revolt by shareholders, many of whom supported the reinstatement of the 63-year-old entrepreneur, could reshape the board as soon as 2027, since all directors stand for reappointment every year. If they are spared, the directors could keep Huang on a much “shorter leash” compared to its history of largely deferring to the overwhelming power of this extraordinary executive, Talley said.

business.title: Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run. Cash and preferred holdings Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change. The company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged. Share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases. Strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing shows no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the company raised no new capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours , and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day. The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Bitcoin liquidations reached about $321 million , with short bets making up $224 million of that total. Liquidations across the broader crypto market topped $762 million. Stocks hold gains as bitcoin fades Stocks kept climbing while bitcoin slid. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% near 24,170 at about 3:40 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained about 5% and the Dow rose about 3.2%. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days before Monday. Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned. A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The dollar index rose about 0.65% to 104.40 , its strongest level since April 2025, as the stock rebound put more Federal Reserve rate hikes back in play. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, pointed to steady selling during U.S. market hours since Huang first stepped down. “Bitcoin has fallen in seven of the eight U.S. sessions since Huang went, today’s included, and last week each session’s fall lined up with that day’s ETF outflow,” he said. Crypto stocks keep most of their gains Crypto stocks held up far better than the bitcoin price. Coinbase (COIN) gained about 6.7% to near $108.78, Robinhood (HOOD) rose about 8.8% to near $67.64 and Circle (CRCL) added about 8% to near $51.33. Miners with AI data center businesses posted the biggest moves. IREN (IREN) jumped about 23% to near $14.57, CleanSpark (CLSK) rose about 12.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) gained about 10%. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. He was named Metro Player and Rookie of the Week on Monday for the third time in as many weeks to begin the season. He's the first Metro freshman to win three Player of the Week honors in an entire season in the 47-year history of the league. "I kind of just try not to look at it," Ibukunoluwa said before practice. "I know what my goal is. My goal is to win every single game, win the Metro and get to the tournament. That (awards) stuff isn't really any of my goals, but obviously, it's nice for it to come with it. So I'm just looking at the wins." Siena fans will get to see the 6-foot-8 Australian phenom in person again when the Saints take on the University of Vermont at 7 p.m. Tuesday at MVP Arena. He's tied for fourth in the country at 25.2 points per game and ranks ninth at 10.5 rebounds per contest. In Saturday's 93-87 win at Bucknell , Ibukunoluwa finished with 34 points, 15 rebounds and six assists to become the first Division I freshman with at least 30 points, 15 rebounds and five assists in a game since the 1938-39 season, when the NCAA Tournament began, according to the data sites CBB Analytics and Stathead. He's the first Metro player in any class to win three straight Player of the Week awards since Iona's Nelly Junior Joseph won four in a row from Dec. 12, 2022 to Jan. 2, 2023. Ibukunoluwa also scored 16 points in last Wednesday's loss at St. John's. "Just staying at a school that's going to have good development, that's going to push me and just to play somewhere I'm very comfortable and that I'm always trying to work and improve myself." sports.description: To whatever extent the words of Rassie Erasmus were lost in translation last week, South Africa used their team announcement press conference on Monday to make a clear point. With Erasmus unable to conduct media duties under the terms of his ban from World Rugby , assistant coach Mzwandile Stick stood in at the Springboks ’ hotel in southwest London – taking questions in English but answering only in Xhosa, his first language. It was explained that the coaching staff wanted to ensure nothing was misinterpreted. With the dedicated Kuhle Sonkosi – a former lock who now works for South African broadcaster SuperSport – acting as an impromptu translator, Stick spent a slightly stilted half-an-hour explaining a heavily-changed team for the Nations Championship final against France. He espoused the virtues of Manu Tshituka, the Congo-born back rower compared to Pieter-Steph du Toit primed for an international debut at Twickenham on Sunday. Mzwandile Stick conducted his press briefing entirely in Xhosa (PA) At one point, Stick cracked a joke about his good looks being the reason he attracted more attention than other coaches from the cameras in Dublin, insisting that it had been a collective effort to replace Erasmus. To Sonkosi’s credit, the remark drew a chuckle even on translation. Clearly, the coach was entitled to converse in his mother tongue if he wished to; South Africa has 12 official languages, of course. As is generally the case, he was engaging company. Stick (left) stood in for Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus (Getty) Yet one could should not shake a slightly peculiar feel. sports.title: Jaime Jaquez Jr. Still Fits Miami Heat Culture Despite Trade
sports.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The trade sent Jaime Jaquez Jr. to Milwaukee, yet the Miami Heat connection never truly broke. He returned to the Kaseya Center on November 18 wearing a Bucks jersey and played with the same grit Miami fans love. With the Heat securing a 137–130 victory, he tallied 10 points and dished out five assists to lead his team in that matchup. According to local reports from Ethan Skolnick, insiders and fans are already anticipating a potential reunion as soon as he becomes available. Jaquez has not lost his edge in his first 18 games with the Bucks. He is averaging 14.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 2.9 assists while shooting 42.5% from three-point range. Yahoo Sports notes that his performance has cemented the view that he personifies the traits characterizing “Heat culture.” This culture relies on physicality, downhill pressure, and a willingness to do the dirty work without needing special plays drawn up. Why The Heat Still Want Him Back Miami values players who fit their specific identity, and Jaquez fits it perfectly. His blue-collar mentality matches the ethos the franchise demands from every single player on the roster. Although the Bucks hold the reins on his restricted free agency and any extension discussions, the connection between his style and Miami’s requirements persists. The front office knows that a player who works hard and plays tough is exactly what they need to win again. Fans will keep watching his progress closely as the season unfolds. Should the trade market change, they seek an opportunity to bring him back to South Florida. His stats show he can score and defend, which are the two most important things for a Heat forward. A Look At The Current Roster The Heat are also finding their own rhythm with other young players. Nikola Jovic is carving out a role thanks to his defensive tenacity, though his shooting splits are still low at 32.4/25.0/78.6. Meanwhile, Davion Mitchell has become a key piece after joining in the Jimmy Butler trade. He is averaging 17 points and 8.6 assists while shooting 51% from the field. Mitchell’s ascent has aided the Heat throughout their ongoing seven-game winning streak. Dwyane Wade praised his work ethic on his YouTube channel, noting that Mitchell travels with a basketball everywhere he goes as a grown man. “A guy that walks around and travel with a basketball everywhere he goes as a grown man, I’m rocking with him,” said Wade. The Heat have a clear path forward with players who love the game and work hard. Whether Jaquez returns or not, the team has found a way to keep its core values alive. The roster is built on players who understand what it takes to succeed in Miami. Jaquez recorded 10 points and five assists in his return game on November 18.

sports.title: Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana hits out at Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe critics and demands respect for 'killer' former PSG superstar
sports.description: Kylian Mbappe - Getty Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has mounted a passionate defence of Kylian Mbappe's Ligue 1 record, insisting his international team-mate's achievements are far too often downplayed. The French centre-back also sparked debate by comparing Mbappe at his peak to Brazilian icon Neymar. Fofana leaps to defence of Mbappe's French legacy Fofana has passionately defended Mbappe's record in Ligue 1, arguing that the forward's achievements in France are frequently trivialised. Speaking as a guest on the YouTube show Zack en Roue Libre , the French centre-back insisted that critics fail to appreciate the true scale of Mbappe's dominance during his time in his homeland. Mbappe rose through the youth academy at Monaco before spending seven prolific years at PSG. Despite his extraordinary goalscoring output across those seasons, Fofana believes public perception has unfairly downplayed his domestic exploits. Chelsea star compares prime Mbappe to Neymar To illustrate Mbappe's brilliance, Fofana weighed the French superstar against his former PSG star Neymar, placing the Brazilian just behind football's two greatest modern icons. However, the Chelsea defender maintained that Mbappe's relentless efficiency in Ligue 1 matched Neymar's peak level. "If you take Mbappe in his prime and Neymar in his prime, it is a close contest," Fofana said. "Neymar is the ultimate player after CR7 and Messi. But what I saw from Mbappe in Ligue 1 was insane. We trivialise what he did far too much." A dominant seven-year spell in the French capital After bursting onto the scene with Monaco, Mbappe seven-year stint at PSG saw him deliver relentless consistency week after week in Ligue 1. Having faced the challenge of defending against top-level attackers himself, Fofana offered a player's perspective on how difficult it is to maintain that standard. By labelling Mbappe a "hitman", the Chelsea defender emphasised the ruthless predictability of his goalscoring rather than sheer spectacle. "Mbappe is a hitman; every weekend it's a goal," he noted. "With Neymar, there is the flair, the madness, because you tell yourself, 'imagine if he had been serious'." Debate continues over Mbappe's place among football's elite Fofana's candid assessment is sure to fuel ongoing debates among supporters regarding how Mbappe's years in France should be judged alongside his peers. What is certain is that Mbappe will continue his campaign with Real Madrid this season, with Los Blancos set to face PSV in the Champions League. sports.description: England’s all-Welsh opening partnership of Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt annihilated Australia with a brutal display of power hitting to level the T20 series in style on the Gold Coast. The pair rained down 13 sixes on the Carrara Oval in a frenzied stand of 151 that saw them make a target of 185 look like child’s play, speeding to an eight-wicket thrashing with 6.5 overs unused. It was a devastating display which left some nasty scars on a pieced-together Australia attack that performed impressively to go 1-0 ahead at the MCG. sports.title: Roma eyeing Sporting Lisbon forward Fotis Ioannidis
sports.description: Roma eyeing Sporting Lisbon forward Fotis Ioannidis Roma continues to monitor the attacking market ahead of the winter transfer window, evaluating various opportunities to strengthen Gian Piero Gasperini’s attack. Following rumors of interest in Endrick, another name has emerged that could fuel competition with AC Milan: Fotis Ioannidis, a 2000-born Greek striker currently playing for Sporting CP. AC Milan is closely monitoring Ioannidis in their search for a centre-forward to replace Camarda, including the Greek among the options being evaluated along with Endrick and Tresoldi. One potential player who could influence AC Milan’s interest is Ruben Amorim, who has previously worked with the striker at Sporting CP and knows his characteristics. According to Gianluca Di Marzio, Roma considers the player an interesting prospect, although they haven’t identified him as a top priority. The European calendar will soon offer the Giallorossi the opportunity to observe the striker firsthand. On December 8th, Ioannidis will face Roma in the Champions League for Sporting CP, a match that could be an important opportunity to assess his qualities. So far, the Greek has made 15 appearances this season, scoring two goals and providing two assists. Gasperini, however, is primarily looking for a winger with acceleration, the ability to beat his man, and the ability to attack space—characteristics different from those of a central striker like the Greek. Therefore, any further exploration of Ioannidis will also depend on the opportunities that arise during the January transfer window.

sports.title: Real Madrid superstar coming to terms with his new reality at the club – report
sports.description: Real Madrid superstar coming to terms with his new reality at the club – report Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has confirmed that Vinicius Jr. will start tonight against PSV Eindhoven, but the past month has done a lot of damage to the player’s status at the club. Serving a long suspension from La Liga for a red card he picked up against Villarreal, the Brazilian star slowly saw his place being taken over by Yan Diomande, whom the manager slowly began viewing as an option on the left flank. With the team’s results also improving after the forced change, it slowly began to become clear that Vinicius was no longer as irreplaceable as he had been over the years. For the first time in years, his place in the starting XI began being called into question. Phase of acceptance As reported by Radio Estadio Noche in a recent update, Vinicius is beginning to come to terms with the new reality around his situation. Diomande is slowly replacing Vinicius. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) He accepts that he is no longer an undisputed starter for Real Madrid, and that he can now be replaced in the dynamics. Needless to say, that requires a massive shift in mentality and a real sense of maturity for a player who has been the face of the club for years. With the acceptance of his situation, Vinicius also now understands that he may have to sit on the bench and watch Diomande as a starter for Real Madrid. Regardless of how mature his understanding may be, it will undoubtedly prick the player to see his spot being owned by a teammate. A hope for resurgence Vinicius had a great international break. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) For a long time, Vinicius’ situation this season seemed hopeless and his arc appeared to only be moving downhill. The recent international break, however, provided a sense of hope for the first time and handed the player a major confidence boost. In Brazil’s two games in the recent hiatus, Vinicius scored five goals including a hat-trick and a brace, putting aside his poor form and rediscovering his goalscoring boots. He started on the bench at the weekend, but his cameo was powerful and even played a critical part in Real Madrid’s comeback. As he prepares to start tonight, the player will be aware that a lot rides on what he makes of the opportunity . After all, he is already treading on a tightrope and is a couple of poor performances from definitely losing his starting spot.

sports.description: Riding a 5–1 High Into Paris: Can Gasperini’s Roma Ambush a Depleted PSG? There’s nothing like a little canapé to tempt the palate, and four goals at the Stadio Ennio Tardini are just that: a great way of sharpening the appetite before a meeting of the heavyweights. With Donyell Malen achieving AS Roma’s first four-goal Serie A appearance since Vincenzo Montella in 2002 – and let’s not forget Rodrigo Mora’s stunning 71’ cherry on top of the cake – there’s a huge amount of momentum under the team’s feet. Now, the Giallorossi carry that momentum to the Parc des Princes on Wednesday for a pivotal Matchday 5 UEFA Champions League clash against two-time defending champions (and daunting foe) Paris Saint-Germain. While Luis Enrique faces his former club amid a 12-match winning streak across all competitions, PSG’s attack has been rocked by consecutive ACL ruptures to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Désiré Doué . There’s a clear opening, and a huge amount of wind in the sails. So, is this the best time to strike? The Stakes in Paris Paris Saint-Germain sit at the top of the league table the 36-team standings at 4–0–0 with 12 points and a +15 goal differential, having piled up 20 goals while conceding five in victories over Barcelona, Manchester City, Villarreal, and Slovan Bratislava. Roma, however, occupy 20th place on four points (1–1–2, +2 goal differential) after falling 3–2 at Manchester United on Matchday 4. There’s a narrative that, taken at face value, doesn’t seem all that promising – tactical dominance vs a desperate fight for survival. And fans are acutely aware that, with only four league-phase fixtures remaining (and a home tie against Sporting CP next on December 8) the margin for error around the top-24 playoff cutoff is shrinking very quickly. Stealing points from the tournament’s pace-setters in Paris would give Gasperini’s squad invaluable cushion heading into winter. Fortunately for Roma, PSG’s double injury blow changes things a lot. Losing both Kvaratskhelia and Doué means that Luis Enrique’s left side has been stripped of vital press-breakers, creating an invitation for Gasperini’s trademark man-oriented pressing. If midfielders Manu Koné and Bryan Cristante can disrupt Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz early, aggressive wing-back overlaps from Molina and Wesley can pin back PSG’s full-backs and overload the channels. Still, surviving the Parc des Princes requires discipline. PSG average 5.0 goals and 57 percent possession per Champions League match, meaning Roma’s back three and in-form goalkeeper Mile Svilar must withstand sustained early pressure. sports.description: Chelsea FC v Manchester United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has opened up on the psychological toll of facing Real Madrid’s elite and the physical battles that nearly drove him out of the game entirely. The Frenchman described a specific Champions League encounter that left him feeling outclassed by the legendary Karim Benzema. Fofana opens up on brutal Bernabeu night Fofana has offered a stark assessment of his experiences facing the world's best, admitting that former Real Madrid captain Benzema left a lasting scar on his professional psyche. Reflecting on Chelsea’s 2023 Champions League quarter-final exit against the Spanish giants, the centre-back confessed to being overwhelmed by the sheer quality on display at the Santiago Bernabeu. The Blues lost both legs 2-0, with Benzema finding the net in the first encounter to set the tone for a dominant Madrid performance. "Benzema traumatised me. He took us out all by himself. Him and Vinícius, it was just nonsense. Rodrygo, he came to finish the job, because I'm not driven by goals. If we talk about football, the two of them, Vinícius and Benzema, it was too much, it was nonsense. We played against Modrić, they had a dream team,” Fofana revealed during an appearance on the YouTube show Zack , as quoted by Foot Mercato . The defender compares England's top flight to Europe The 25-year-old defender was quick to point out that while competing in England’s top flight demands an elite standard, stepping onto Europe’s biggest stage is a different beast altogether. Even with the prestige of representing a heavyweight like Chelsea, he admitted that facing continental royalty at the Santiago Bernabeu served as a stark reality check. "We went to play at the Santiago Bernabeu and they gave us a football lesson. Chelsea is a high level. You're in a big club, the Premier League is a high level, you're in a big league. But the Champions League is even higher. It’s higher still," Fofana added. The brink of early retirement Beyond the challenges on the pitch, Fofana’s time in West London has been heavily disrupted by a series of long-term fitness issues. The Frenchman has missed a staggering 696 days of action due to various ailments since moving to Stamford Bridge, including a significant ACL injury that sidelined him for nearly a year. These recurring setbacks eventually led him to a dark place where he seriously considered tearing up his contract and walking away from professional football for good. The defender reached a breaking point during the 2024-25 season while working under manager Enzo Maresca. After recovering from major knee surgery, he suffered consecutive thigh injuries that made him feel as though his body was fundamentally broken. sports.description: Newcastle United v Arsenal FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Bruno Guimaraes revealed Mikel Arteta immediately challenged him to help create a dynasty at Arsenal when he arrived from Newcastle United this summer. Ahead of Tuesday's Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund, the Brazilian midfielder insisted he still has another level to reach alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard. Guimaraes reveals Arteta's dynasty message Bruno Guimaraes has helped propel Arsenal to the top of the Premier League and an unbeaten Champions League league phase since arriving from Newcastle United this summer, yet he insists the best is still to come. Speaking to the media on Monday ahead of Tuesday night's meeting with Borussia Dortmund at Emirates Stadium, the Brazilian shared the ambitious mandate Mikel Arteta gave him upon signing . "We want to make a dynasty here; we want to win everything possible," Guimaraes said. "I think since I came to the club, the first thing Mikel said to me was create a dynasty for the club, so we want to win everything that's possible." Adapting to a freer role in midfield Despite scoring twice early in his Arsenal career and becoming an instant favourite with supporters, Guimaraes explained that adjusting to Arteta's fluid midfield demands has pushed him harder than ever. Playing across the number six, eight and nine spaces requires constant movement, and he leans heavily on Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard to sharpen his positioning. "It's very different, here is a little bit more free. You play as a six, an eight, and a nine sometimes, so we have to move a lot, and of course I was not used to it," Guimaraes said. Praising his midfield partners, he added: "They're both amazing players. I think Declan is a monster, he can run 15 kilometres in a game, and Martin Odegaard, he always can find space to penetrate the opposite side." Squad competition and European milestones With Martin Zubimendi and Bukayo Saka ruled out for the next few weeks with muscle injuries and David Raya sidelined by a shoulder issue, Guimaraes stressed that internal competition keeps standards high across the dressing room. sports.title: Sean McVay says he’s ‘excited’ about Rams after season-ending injury to Puka Nacua
sports.description: Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are losing their star receiver for the season, but head coach Sean McVay is still excited for one key reason. The Los Angeles Rams are currently sitting at 6-4 in a tough division with the rampaging San Francisco 49ers and the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks. The team has had their share of injury issues pop up, most notably to star receiver Puka Nacua. In seven games this season, Nacua was averaging 10 receptions and just over 100 receiving yards per game. Nacua was initially diagnosed with multiple ligament sprains and turf toe after being injured on LA’s final offensive snap in Week 9 against the Commanders. Since then, it has been revealed that he will undergo MCL surgery and miss the rest of the season. Head coach Sean McVay is still ‘excited’. Sean McVay says he is ‘excited’ to see how the LA Rams respond to adversity and how other players step up Nacua being out isn’t the only concern plaguing McVay at the minute. Davante Adams has been out injured, and now even tight end Terrance Ferguson is set to undergo season-ending surgery. Their receiving options are looking extremely light at the minute, but McVay seems to have belief in his guys. Asked about the situation by The Athletic’s Nate Atkins, the head coach gave a surprising answer sharing his positive outlook regarding the remainder of the season. “Based on last week, I’m excited about what those guys that did get opportunities did,” McVay said. “Let’s continue to see if we can grow and figure out what it looks like. You know the information that I had at the time, but I don’t want it to ever be misunderstood. “I am confident in Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield and Xavier Smith and C.J. Daniels, and (Brennan) Presley getting a chance to get back there and return kicks. It’s a bummer to lose those two significant pieces, but I think you have to adjust and adapt. “This is the hand that we’re dealt. I’m excited about trying to watch these guys go shine and do everything we can with our decision-making and our thought process to help bring that to life collectively for our group. A lot of that stuff, there have been some moving parts. “The Terrance Ferguson stuff I just found out 30 minutes ago. technology.title: Education software supplier's legacy login system left 355,000 school email addresses exposed
technology.description: More than 355,000 school staff and pupil email addresses ended up in the hands of hackers who broke into UK education software supplier Bromcom in September. The breach was added to Have I Been Pwned on Monday, revealing that 355,051 unique email addresses were caught up in the incident. The data also included single sign-on (SSO) registration reference numbers, although Bromcom insists that no passwords or authentication tokens were stolen. As The Register reported in Octobe r , the attackers got in through a legacy SSO registration component in Bromcom's Communications Server environment. The technology had already been superseded but was still running because an internal system continued to use it. Bromcom discovered something was amiss on September 6 after customers reported problems accessing its SSO service. At the time, the company was still working with external forensic specialists to establish exactly what the intruders had managed to get their hands on. Bromcom's FAQ says its investigation is complete and confirms that the intruders used a script to extract SSO registration information from the compromised server. The supplier insists its Management Information System (MIS), used by schools to keep track of everything from attendance to pupil records, was untouched. The compromised service also couldn't be used to get into Microsoft or Google accounts, which have their own login systems. Bromcom has since pulled the plug on the old component, tightened its authorization checks, and added more security logging. It says it hasn't found any evidence of accounts being hijacked as a result of the breach. Bromcom also confirmed it hadn't reported the breach to the UK's Information Commission's Office. Its reasoning is that it was the data processor, not the controller, so any decision to involve the regulator was for the affected schools and academy trusts to make. As for the risk to staff and pupils, Bromcom considers it to be low. No passwords or pupil records held in the MIS were taken, it says, although schools have been advised to watch for phishing messages and suspicious requests to reset passwords or approve sign-ins. The supplier's software is used by more than 5,000 schools and 390 multi-academy trusts across the UK, though it hasn't said how many were caught up in this particular mess. The Register has asked Bromcom how many schools and pupils were affected, and whether the figure published by Have I Been Pwned matches its own findings, but has yet to receive a response. Bromcom kept the superseded component running because an internal system still needed it. Unfortunately, the intruders found a use for it too. ®

technology.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
technology.description: Cisco and OpenAI have released an open-source tool called Shirudo to implement compensating controls in Linux, potentially improving security for users who can’t quickly patch newly discovered software flaws. Shirudo relies on eBPF, the technology that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel. eBPF programs are effectively kernel plug-ins but don’t get unrestricted access to system resources. Developers have mostly used eBPF to create network functions that enable things like the open source Kubernetes observability and security tool Cilium , a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project. Cisco and OpenAI think eBPF can help organizations cope with the flood of 100,000-plus software flaws reported this year, many after the debut of AI-powered bug finders. The increased volume of flaws, and patches to fix them, is a problem for many organizations which already struggle to test fixes or find change windows in which to implement them. That problem has seen greater interest in “compensating controls” – changes to applications or infrastructure that harden them against flaws or malware, without requiring a patch. With Shirudo, Cisco and OpenAI are suggesting two things: The privileges eBPF programs enjoy make them a fine way to implement compensating controls for Linux; Agents should scan your infrastructure for vulnerabilities, then use tools like OpenAI’s Codex to write compensating controls as eBPF programs at machine speed. “Shirudo” is apparently the Japanese word for “shield,” so Cisco and OpenAI have called the eBPF programs the tool creates “shields.” The two companies envision humans checking every shield Shirudo creates before putting it into production. Shirudo is open source and available here . The two companies say they’ve already demonstrated it could mitigate the recently discovered flaws in Java without requiring downtime for an Elasticsearch implementation. Cisco and OpenAI are not alone in advocating for compensating controls. Third-party software maintenance outfits like Rimini Street have used them for years to protect software when their clients no longer have the right to access patches. VMware has introduced “virtual patching.” Palo Alto Networks and Rapid 7 also like this approach, and offer automation to develop controls. Where Cisco and OpenAI differ is their decision to make Shirudo open source , and their ambition that other players adapt and advance it. That offer is not entirely altruistic, as if Shirudo takes off it could create more demand for Codex. Cisco’s angle comes from the fact it owns Isovalent, an early champion of eBPF and the creator of both Cilium and the Tetragon sub-project on which Shirudo is based. Switchzilla is using eBPF in other products, so normalizing its use through an open source project can’t hurt. ®

But if the AI can’t explain what it’s “proven,” are we actually any closer to understanding anything, or have we simply built another black box? That question is top of mind among mathematicians and computer scientists this week after Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved a mathematical conjecture so elusive it's gone unproven for more than 150 years. The fact that this note came out one day after Anthropic's record-setting IPO is a coincidence, we're sure. In a four-page post to his website, the researcher described how with the help of Claude, he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, one of seven Millennium problems so complex and so important that the Clay Mathematics Institute has offered a $1 million prize to anyone who is successful in solving them. The Riemann Hypothesis, conjectured by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, contends that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function – those with a real part between zero and one – have a real part equal to 1/2. Confused? Don’t worry. We’ve linked to an explainer that goes into more detail here . What's important is that, if the Riemann Hypothesis is right, mathematicians can place tighter bounds on the difference between the actual distribution of prime numbers and mathematical estimates of that distribution. Researchers have previously attempted to disprove the conjecture through computational brute force, and therein have shown the hypothesis holds to at least 10 trillion zeros . There’s reason to believe that the Riemann Hypothesis is accurate, but the possibility remains that over a sufficiently long series the pattern might diverge. And so, more than 150 years after Riemann published his hypothesis, it has remained just that. Alpöge’s proof, if it can even be called that, is now the subject of great debate. technology.description: Don't mind the recent arrests. The ShinyHunters extortion gang may still be operating, just under the new name of Inception, according to Okta's threat intelligence group. ShinyHunters is the brash cybercriminal group that, most recently, breached rival gang Clop before hacking the FBI , resulting in at least three arrests of key suspects in September and October. The crims - and their old data leak site - have since gone dark. “While this threat cluster has changed their brand affiliation, the operators remain active in targeting organizations with voice phishing attacks and account takeovers resulting in data theft and extortion,” Okta threat hunters Moussa Diallo and Katie Nickels said on Monday. Okta tracks this threat cluster as O-UNC-053 - the “O-UNC” prefix stands for an Okta Uncategorized cluster, and it uses this label before formally attributing the activity to a named threat group. While Okta hasn't formally confirmed O-UNC-053 to be the same crime crew as ShinyHunters, the identity and access management provider’s researchers note that it does use nearly identical social engineering tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA). Plus, they note: O-UNC-053 operators change the themes of their phishing domains about every four to six weeks, and they also post claimed victims on ShinyHunters’ data leak site. In November, however, organizations targeted by O-UNC-053 began appearing on a new data leak site branded as Inception and not ShinyHunters. technology.title: Amazon scoops up AI accelerator tech to keep chips busy at all times
technology.description: Amazon has agreed to buy AI optimization technology from an Israeli startup in a bid to speed up its inference operations. The house of Bezos on Monday announced a deal to purchase proprietary AI acceleration tech from Decart AI, known as the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), for an undisclosed amount. Amazon also plans to bring Decart’s three founders and their engineering team into the fold. Decart’s DOS is designed to push AI hardware closer to its maximum performance across different AI models and hardware platforms. The company claims that most AI chips live their lives without reaching their full potential – practically a sin in this age of increased hardware costs and limited availability – and DOS aims to fix that by operating between the model and the chip, optimizing kernels, compilers, and runtimes for the underlying hardware “so every core stays busy.” DOS is hardware-agnostic, with Decart saying it supports Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and, most critically for our purposes here, AWS Trainium chips. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost,” Peter DeSantis, Amazon SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, and quantum computing, said in the announcement. “That's the pillar Trainium and our AI efforts are built on, and from our earliest work with Decart, we knew they … would help us push it even further.” Decart doesn’t offer much in the way of details about its proprietary AI-maxxing tech, but claims it can reduce latency, improve throughput, and reduce the costs associated with training and inference runs. An Amazon spokesperson clarified to The Register that the deal is an asset purchase and not a full company acquisition, with Amazon only acquiring DOS and the tech behind it as well as personnel. As for what may become of Decart after the deal, that’s unclear. Amazon told us to reach out to Decart to learn what may happen to any remaining employees and the company’s other technology, but we didn’t hear back. Along with offering its optimization stack, Decart has a couple of different AI models: Lucy, a live video model marketed toward advertisers, live streamers, and the like; and Oasis, a world model AI marketed toward companies working on embodied AI applications. Decart’s non-DOS assets weren’t mentioned in the press release, and per the Amazon spokesperson we talked to, that means they weren’t part of the deal. We can’t imagine that the Decart team is too upset about the potential abandonment of those models, though: While neither company has disclosed a price, Bloomberg claims its sources value the deal at around $7.5 billion. If Bloomberg's figure is accurate, that would make this deal one of the most expensive in Amazon’s history, right between its $3.9 billion acquisition of One Medical and its $8.5 billion purchase of film studio MGM . ®
